# Fälligkeitsdatum für Todos

Ticket: #1 – Fälligkeitsdatum für Todos

## Intent and scope

Todos may optionally have a due date so API consumers and readers of the list can identify overdue work. The user confirmed that a due date is a calendar day without a time. An open todo is overdue exactly when its due date precedes today's UTC date. Undated and completed todos are never overdue. The visible label must be exactly `überfällig`.

## Approaches

1. Compute `overdue` in the API on every response and have the list consume that value. Recommended and selected by the user: one authoritative UTC rule.
2. Compute overdue status separately in the API and browser. Rejected because this duplicates the rule and risks inconsistent results.

## API and data

- Builder proposal: all todo representations include `dueDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD` or `null`) and `overdue` (boolean), alongside the existing fields.
- POST and PATCH accept an optional `dueDate`. Omission on POST means `null`; omission on PATCH preserves the existing date. Explicit `null` removes the date.
- Accept only real calendar dates with a four-digit year from 0001 through 9999. Reject invalid days, wrong formats, timestamps, and other JSON types with `ValidationError`, mapped to HTTP 400.
- Calculate `overdue` when producing a todo response, never persist it. Changing the current UTC day or toggling completion must affect subsequent responses immediately.
- `GET /todos?overdue=true` returns only todos whose computed `overdue` is true. Without this flag the endpoint returns all todos in the existing order. Only the exact value `true` activates the filter; `false` and other values leave the list unfiltered.
- Validate the complete patch before changing a todo so rejected updates leave its fields unchanged.

## List

- Keep the existing read-only list and title/completion display.
- Builder proposal: display a dated todo's date as `YYYY-MM-DD` in a semantic `time` element. Show a separate `überfällig` label only when the API reports `overdue: true`.
- Add an initially unchecked checkbox labeled exactly `nur überfällige`, with `data-testid="overdue-filter"`. Checking it reloads the list from `/todos?overdue=true`; unchecking it reloads `/todos`. The selected state must remain authoritative even if requests finish out of order.
- Give the new date and label elements `data-testid="todo-due-date"` and `data-testid="todo-overdue"`.
- Use text nodes/textContent for values. No create/edit forms, sorting, reminders, styling, persistence, or new dependencies.

## Verification

- Use TDD with Node's built-in test runner. Cover date validation (including leap years), absent/null dates, PATCH semantics and atomicity, UTC boundaries, completion changes, derived status on all todo API response routes, and filtering (including no matches).
- The user explicitly requested agent-run end-to-end testing. Start the app following AGENTS.md and drive the list with Playwright MCP tools. Seed todos through the API; verify past, today, future, completed, and undated cases; verify date changes/removal after reload and exact lowercase `überfällig` text. Toggle `nur überfällige` on and off and check the matching list, including an empty result. Save screenshot evidence outside the repository and stop the app afterwards.

## Consequences and constraints

Node 24 built-ins only, with the existing in-memory lifetime. The response schema gains two fields, including for existing undated todos. Clients must tolerate those added fields. No automatic refresh is introduced; the list reflects the status returned at page load.

The implementation may choose internal helpers and clock injection for deterministic tests. The chosen public behavior and UTC date semantics are fixed by this design once approved.

## Implementation Summary

**Approach** — Optionale Fälligkeitsdaten werden im Store validiert. Die API berechnet `overdue` bei jeder Todo-Antwort anhand des aktuellen UTC-Tags. Die Liste zeigt das Datum, die Kennzeichnung `überfällig` und eine Checkbox `nur überfällige`, die den API-Filter verwendet.

**Consequences** — Todo-Antworten enthalten zusätzlich `dueDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD` oder `null`) und `overdue` (Boolean). POST/PATCH setzen das Datum; PATCH mit `null` entfernt es, ein ausgelassenes Feld erhält es. `GET /todos?overdue=true` liefert ausschließlich offene Todos mit einem Datum vor heute (UTC). Ungültige Kalenderdaten ergeben HTTP 400; abgelehnte Updates verändern keine Felder.

**Possible side effects** — API-Clients sehen zwei zusätzliche Antwortfelder. Die Liste aktualisiert sich beim Laden und Filterwechsel. Daten bleiben wie bisher im Arbeitsspeicher. Keine Sortierung, Erinnerungen, Styling oder neuen Abhängigkeiten.

**Watch when testing** — 19 Node-Tests bestanden, einschließlich Schaltjahren, UTC-Mitternacht und atomaren Updates. End to end durch den Agenten mit Playwright getestet: Vergangenheit/heute/Zukunft, erledigte/undatierte Todos, exakte Beschriftungen, Filter an/aus/leeres Ergebnis, Datum ändern/entfernen, erledigen/wiederöffnen sowie schnelle Filterwechsel mit verzögerten Antworten in beiden Richtungen. HTML im Titel bleibt Text. App anschließend beendet. Nachweis: erfolgreiche Browser-Assertions und Beobachtungen; Screenshots außerhalb des Repositorys wurden vom Browser-Werkzeug verweigert.
